verdict.rationale: Granola documents its own self-serve CSV export, an open format, covering note titles, summaries, transcripts and basic details. The docs pitch it for backups, migration and GDPR portability, and a REST API (Business/Enterprise only) exposes notes, transcripts and folders. However, the CSV covers only "basic details", so the docs do not show that *all* data can be exported. Missing for 10: documented export of all data types (shared-screen snapshots, raw notes, folder/space structure, templates, recipes), richer open formats such as Markdown or JSON beyond CSV, a documented account-deletion/offboarding path, and independent hands-on confirmation of a complete export.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: The CSV includes the title, note summary, transcript, and other basic details for each note.
Useful for backups, migration, or GDPR data portability requests.
You're able to export historical data from Granola by going to Settings, clicking Profile in the sidebar (under Preferences), and clicking Generate CSV
The Granola API lets you build custom integrations with programmatic access to meeting notes, transcripts, and AI summaries.
